sentences.text:
Naresh Pal Singh And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on
17 May, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 14806 of 2023
Applicant :- Naresh Pal Singh And 3 Others

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Daya Shanker Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr. P.C. has been filed to quash the chargesheet dated 02.12.2021 in Case Crime No. 168 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 354 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mahua Khera, District Aligarh and summoning order dated 19.01.2022 passed by learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Aligarh.
Learned counsel for the applicants submit that summoning order appended at page 55 of the paper book, is a cryptic order passed on a prescribed format by filling the blanks.

The order itself shows that there was no application of mind by learned Magistrate while passing the order dated 19.01.2022, hence prayer is made accordingly.
So far as the argument that the cognizance order has been passed on a printed proforma is concerned, although it has been held by this Court in the case of Megh Nath Gupta & another Vs.
Naresh Pal Singh And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165128465/
1 State of U.P. and another, 2008 (62) ACC 826 that the Magistrate is not required to pass detailed reasoned order at the time of taking cognizance on the charge-sheet, but it does not mean that order of taking cognizance can be passed by filling up the blanks on printed proforma.

entities.text:
Megh Nath Gupta & another Vs.
Naresh Pal Singh And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of passing any judicial order including the order taking cognizance on the charge-sheet, the court is required to apply its judicial mind and even the order of taking cognizance cannot be passed in mechanical manner.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Harischandra Prasad Mani and others Vs.
State of Jharkhand and another (2007) 15 Supreme Court Cases 494, Fakhruddin Ahmad Vs. State of Uttaranchal and another (2008) 17 Supreme Court Cases 157 and Ankit Vs. State of U.P. and others, U.P. Criminal Report 2009 (3) 427 has established that if the order on printed proforma is passed it establishes that the Magistrate concerned has not applied his mind to the evidence on record in order to take cognizance of the offence concerned.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case also the cognizance order has been passed by the Magistrate concerned on a printed proforma just by filling the blanks which clearly shows that the Magistrate concerned did not apply his judicial mind and had not gone through the material evidence on record while passing the order.
As a result the cognizance order, which has been passed by filling the blanks on the printed proforma is found to be a cryptic order, which cannot be sustained.
Hence, the impugned cognizance order is liable to be quashed.
Without going into the merits of the case the cognizance order dated 19.01.2022, is hereby quashed.
The trial court court is directed to pass a detailed and reasoned, fresh order within one month regarding cognizance as per law.
The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is disposed of, accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Harischandra Prasad Mani and others Vs.
State of Jharkhand and another (2007) 15 Supreme Court Cases 494, Fakhruddin Ahmad Vs. State of Uttaranchal and another (2008) 17 Supreme Court Cases 157 and Ankit Vs. State of U.P. and others, U.P. Criminal Report 2009 (3) 427 has established that if the order on printed proforma is passed it establishes that the Magistrate concerned has not applied his mind to the evidence on record in order to take cognizance of the offence concerned.
In the present case also the cognizance order has been passed by the Magistrate concerned on a printed proforma just by filling the blanks which clearly shows that the Magistrate concerned did not apply his judicial mind and had not gone through the material evidence on record while passing the order.
As a result the cognizance order, which has been passed by filling the blanks on the printed proforma is found to be a cryptic order, which cannot be sustained.
